content: Everything happens for a reason. This is called CAUSE and EFFECT.

Sentence: The streets were flooded BECAUSE it rained heavily.
Or: It rained heavily, SO the streets were flooded.
Sentence: He got good grades BECAUSE he studied hard.
Or: He studied hard, SO he got good grades.

listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
Everything happens for a reason. This is called CAUSE and EFFECT.
The CAUSE is the reason WHY something happens.
The EFFECT is WHAT happens.
Example 1:
CAUSE: It rained heavily.
EFFECT: The streets were flooded.
Sentence: The streets were flooded BECAUSE it rained heavily.
Or: It rained heavily, SO the streets were flooded.
Example 2:
CAUSE: The boy studied hard.
EFFECT: He got good grades.
Sentence: He got good grades BECAUSE he studied hard.
Or: He studied hard, SO he got good grades.
"Because" introduces the CAUSE (reason).
"So" introduces the EFFECT (result).
Can you find the cause and effect in your daily life?
dictation: This is called CAUSE and EFFECT.
The CAUSE is the reason WHY something happens.

The Language of "Carrying Over"
When we add big numbers, sometimes we need to CARRY OVER.
Look at this problem: 28 + 15 = ?
Step 1: Add the ONES column.
8 + 5 = 13
13 is more than 10!
Step 2: CARRY OVER the 1 to the TENS column.
Write 3 in the ones place.
Carry 1 to t
